region: Arid and steppe belt: Arabian Peninsula, North African interior, Central Asia and steppe, Siberia, Mongolia and Tibet frontier

polities.name: Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State)
polities.note: Town emirate of Al Saud until the 1744 alliance with Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab; Riyadh taken 1773, al-Hasa c.1795, Mecca 1803/1806, Medina 1805; destroyed by Egyptian-Ottoman army 1818. Main extent = c.1800 (Najd + Hasa).

polities.name: Emirate of Nejd (Second Saudi State)
polities.note: Al-Hasa held 1830-1871 (lost to Ottomans 1871); civil war of Faisal's sons from 1865; Rashidi overlordship from 1887, Al Saud expelled after Mulayda 1891 (Riyadh then governed by Rashidi governors until 1902).

polities.name: Emirate of al-Uyaynah
polities.note: Oasis emirate of the Al Mu'ammar, the leading town of al-Arid in the 15th-17th c.; absorbed by Diriyah after 1750-60. Start date approximate.

polities.name: Diriyah town emirate (Al Muqrin)
polities.note: Founded 1446 by Mani' al-Muraydi, ancestor of Al Saud; one of many small Najdi town-states before 1727 (continues as Emirate of Diriyah).

polities.name: Emirate of Riyadh (Al Dawwas)
polities.note: Dahham ibn Dawwas ruled Riyadh/Manfuha and fought Diriyah for c.27 years; fled 1773.

polities.name: Emirate of Jabal Shammar
polities.note: Al Rashid of the Shammar; al-Jawf added 1853; peak under Muhammad ibn Rashid (1869-97) ruling all Najd after 1891; conquered by Ibn Saud 1921.

polities.name: Emirate of Buraydah (Qassim)
polities.note: Northern Qassim town emirate (Al Abu Ulayyan, then Al Muhanna from 1860s); rival of Unaizah; dates approximate.

polities.name: Emirate of Unaizah
polities.note: Southern Qassim trading town under its own amirs (Al Sulaim in 19th c.); dates approximate.

polities.name: Sharifate of Mecca

overlord.name: Egypt (Muhammad Ali) for the Ottoman Empire

polities.note: Hashemite sharifs governed Mecca, Ta'if and much of Hejaz; Medina and Jeddah usually under separate Mamluk/Ottoman officials. Independent Kingdom of Hejaz 1916-1925.

polities.name: Emirate of the Banu Khalid
polities.note: Al Humaid of the Banu Khalid expelled the Ottomans from al-Hasa 1669/70; overlords of Qatif, Hasa and the Kuwait coast; conquered by the First Saudi State 1793-96, briefly restored 1818-1830.

polities.name: Jabrid Sultanate
polities.note: Bedouin dynasty of the Banu Uqayl ruling al-Hasa, Qatif and (from 1487) Bahrain; also raided into Oman; fell to Muntafiq/Portuguese-Hormuz pressure c.1521-24.

polities.name: Lahsa Eyalet (Ottoman al-Hasa)
polities.note: Ottoman province of eastern Arabia, coast and al-Hasa oasis; lost to the Banu Khalid c.1670.

polities.name: Hasa Sanjak (Ottoman)
polities.note: Ottoman (Basra vilayet) sanjak taken from the Second Saudi State 1871; taken by Ibn Saud 1913.

polities.name: Emirate of Asir (Al Mutahami / Al A'id)
polities.note: Highland chiefs of the Asir confederation (Rufaydah/Mughaydi) who joined the Wahhabis, resisted Egypt in the 1820s-30s and were annexed by the Ottomans 1871-72. Before 1800 Asir was tribal (see gaps).

polities.name: Makrami Emirate of Najran
polities.note: Sulaymani Isma'ili da'is of the Al Makrami family, backed by the Yam tribe, ruled Najran from the mid-17th c. and raided Hadramawt and Najd; annexed by Saudi Arabia 1934. Start date approximate.

polities.name: Sheikhdom of Kuwait
polities.note: Utub settlement under Al Sabah; 1899 Anglo-Kuwaiti agreement.

polities.name: Zubarah (Al Khalifa / Utub)
polities.note: Utub (Al Khalifa, Al Jalahma) pearling port on NW Qatar; base for the 1783 conquest of Bahrain; destroyed 1878 by the Al Thani.

polities.name: Bahrain (Al Khalifa)
polities.note: Island archipelago; also claimed NW Qatar (Zubarah) until 1868. British protection formalised 1861/1880/1892.

polities.name: Bahrain under foreign rule
polities.note: Use for the archipelago before Al Khalifa conquest.

polities.name: Qatar (Al Thani)
polities.note: Before 1868 the peninsula's towns were under Bahraini (Al Khalifa) nominal authority and local tribes (Al Musallam, Al Bin Ali).

polities.name: Anazzah confederation
polities.note: Great camel-herding confederation; migrated from Khaybar/northern Hejaz into the Syrian desert in 17th-18th c. Al Saud claim Anazzah descent.

polities.name: Shammar confederation (Jazira branch)
polities.note: Shammar clans (Jarba) who left Najd in the late 18th c. and dominated the Jazira steppe between Euphrates and Tigris; the Najdi Shammar are under the Emirate of Jabal Shammar.

polities.name: Mutayr
polities.note: Camel-herding tribe ranging between Qassim and the Kuwait hinterland (dirah from 18th c.).

polities.name: Utaybah
polities.note: Large confederation of the Najd-Hejaz borderland (between Ta'if and Riyadh).

polities.name: Harb
polities.note: Controlled the Mecca-Medina pilgrim road (received sharifian/Ottoman subsidies); later also in Qassim.

polities.name: Al Murrah
polities.note: Nomads of the northern Rub' al-Khali and Jabrin.

polities.name: Al Ajman (tribe)
polities.note: Yam-descended tribe of the eastern Najd/al-Hasa steppe.

polities.name: Dawasir
polities.note: Settled and nomadic tribe of Wadi ad-Dawasir and al-Aflaj.

polities.name: Qahtan (tribe)
polities.note: Southern Najd and eastern Asir; parts moved to central Najd in the 19th c.

polities.name: Huwaitat
polities.note: Northern Hejaz, Hisma and southern Transjordan; nominally Ottoman.

polities.name: Dhafir
polities.note: Steppe between Kuwait, Zubair and Najd; allied variously with Muntafiq and Saudis.

polities.name: Rasulid Sultanate
polities.note: Lowland and southern Yemen (Tihama, Ta'izz, Ibb, Aden); Zabid winter capital; northern highlands under the Zaydi imams.

polities.name: Tahirid Sultanate
polities.note: Successors of the Rasulids (Zabid, Aden, Ta'izz, Rada'); overthrown by the Mamluk expedition 1517; remnant in Aden until 1538.

polities.name: Zaydi Imamate of Yemen (pre-Qasimid)
polities.note: Rival Zaydi imams (e.g. al-Mahdi Ahmad, Sharaf al-Din line at Thula/Kawkaban 1506-1567) held the northern highlands, Sanaa intermittently. Seat moved (Sa'dah, Thula, Sanaa).

polities.name: Yemen Eyalet (Ottoman, first period)
polities.note: Ottoman Yemen 1538-1635 (highlands only after 1547, lost progressively to the Qasimids from 1597).

polities.name: Yemen Vilayet (Ottoman, second period)
polities.note: Tihama from 1849, Sanaa and highlands from 1872; northern Zaydi highlands under Hamid al-Din imams in revolt from 1890s.

polities.name: Qasimid Imamate of Yemen
polities.note: Expelled the Ottomans 1635/36; at peak (1658-c.1700) ruled Hadramawt and Aden; lost the south to Lahej and Yafa after 1728, Tihama to the Ottomans 1849, Sanaa 1872. Zaydi imamate revived in the northern highlands 1890s-1918 (Hamid al-Din) under Ottoman rule.

polities.name: Sharifate of Abu Arish
polities.note: Sharifs of the Tihama coast north of Hodeidah (Jizan); autonomous from the Zaydi imams in the 18th c., briefly great under Hamud Abu Mismar (1801-1818); then Egyptian/Ottoman.

polities.name: Sultanate of Lahej
polities.note: Broke from the Zaydi imams 1728; held Aden until British seizure 1839.

polities.name: Aden Settlement (British)
polities.note: Taken from Lahej 1839; port and hinterland enclave.

polities.name: Fadhli Sultanate
polities.note: Abyan coast; seat later Zinjibar. Founding date approximate.

polities.name: Lower Yafa Sultanate
polities.note: Yafa'i tribes threw off Zaydi rule c.1700-1730; early seat al-Qara in the Yafa hills; capital Ja'ar in the 19th-20th c.

polities.name: Upper Yafa Sultanate
polities.note: Confederation of Yafa'i sheikhdoms (Mausatta, Dhubi, Hadrami, Maflahi, Dhanbi) under the Harharah sultans.

polities.name: Upper Aulaqi Sultanate
polities.note: Awlaqi tribal sultanate; also Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom (Said) nearby.

polities.name: Wahidi Sultanates
polities.note: Wahidi sultanates of Balhaf, Azzan, Bir Ali and Habban (one family, several branches).

polities.name: Kathiri Sultanate
polities.note: Ruled Wadi Hadramawt with Ash-Shihr (from 1460s) and intermittently Dhofar (seized 1414); first state collapsed 1730 amid Yafa'i incursions; revived 1803; after 1858-81 confined to Seiyun-Tarim by the Qu'aiti.

polities.name: Qu'aiti Sultanate
polities.note: Yafa'i jamadar family enriched in Hyderabad; took Ash-Shihr 1866 and Mukalla 1881 from the Kasadi.

polities.name: Kasadi Sultanate of Mukalla
polities.note: Yafa'i Kasadi naqibs ruled Mukalla port; ousted by the Qu'aiti 1881.

polities.name: Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra
polities.note: Lost Shihr 1495; thereafter mainland Mahra plus the island of Socotra (seat Hadibu/Tamrida, 12.65N 54.02E), settled c.1480; Portuguese fort on Socotra 1507-11.

polities.name: Nabhani dynasty (Oman)
polities.note: Maliks of interior Oman (Bahla, Nizwa) alternating with Ibadi imams; coast under Hormuz then Portugal.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hormuz
polities.note: Maritime kingdom at the Strait; held Omani coastal towns (Qalhat, Muscat, Sohar, Julfar), Bahrain to 1487/1521 and the Persian littoral. Draw as coastal strips; ended by Anglo-Persian capture 1622.

polities.name: Portuguese Muscat and Omani coast
polities.note: Fortified ports Muscat, Sohar, Qurayyat, Khor Fakkan, Julfar; Muscat taken by the Ya'rubids 1650.

polities.name: Ya'rubid Imamate of Oman
polities.note: Expelled the Portuguese (Muscat 1650) and built an overseas empire in East Africa (Mombasa 1698, Zanzibar); civil war from 1719 and Persian invasion 1737-44.

polities.name: Muscat and Oman (Al Busaid)
polities.note: Ahmad bin Said; Zanzibar split off 1856/61; Gwadar 1783-1958; Dhofar (Salalah) held from 1829, firmly from 1879. Interior tribes often autonomous (Azzan's imamate 1868-71).

polities.name: Shihuh of Musandam
polities.note: Mountain tribe of the Musandam peninsula.

polities.name: Qawasim Sheikhdom of Sharjah and Ras al-Khaimah
polities.note: Maritime power also holding Lingeh on the Persian coast; British campaigns 1809, 1819. Ras al-Khaimah separate 1869-1900 and from 1921; Sharjah phase extent excludes RAK.

polities.name: Ras al-Khaimah (separate sheikhdom)
polities.note: Separate Qasimi branch 1869-1900, reabsorbed by Sharjah, independent again 1921.

polities.name: Abu Dhabi (Bani Yas)
polities.note: Bani Yas confederation of Liwa; Abu Dhabi island settled 1761, seat from 1793; Buraimi/al-Ain shared with Oman.

polities.name: Dubai
polities.note: Al Bu Falasah (Al Maktoum) seceded from Abu Dhabi 1833.

polities.name: Fujairah (Sharqiyin)

overlord.name: Qawasim Sheikhdom of Sharjah and Ras al-Khaimah (nominal)

polities.note: Sharqiyin tribe on the Batinah/east coast; de facto autonomous from Sharjah from c.1901; British recognition 1952.

polities.name: Tuat-Gourara-Tidikelt oases
polities.note: Ksour communities under councils (jama'a) and local caids; Tamentit main ksar (Gourara seat Timimoun 29.26N 0.24E; Tidikelt seat In Salah 27.20N 2.47E). Also paid tribute to Algiers until 1830. French occupation 1899-1901.

polities.name: Mzab confederation
polities.note: Ibadi city-league of Ghardaia, Beni Isguen, Melika, Bou Noura, El Atteuf (plus Guerrara and Berriane in the 17th c.); annexed to French Algeria 1882.

polities.name: Sultanate of Ouargla
polities.note: Oasis town with its own sultans (often of disputed authority) between Mzab and Touggourt; French occupation 1853, definitive 1872.

polities.name: Sultanate of Touggourt
polities.note: Banu Djellab dynasty ruling the Oued Righ oases and often the Souf (El Oued); French 1854.

polities.name: Chaamba confederation
polities.note: Arab nomads of the northern Algerian Sahara (Metlili, Ouargla, El Golea); allies of France from the 1850s.

polities.name: Kel Ahaggar
polities.note: Tuareg drum-group (ettebel) confederation under an amenokal (Kel Ghela); submitted to France 1905.

polities.name: Kel Ajjer
polities.note: Tuareg confederation of the Tassili n'Ajjer; Ghat (Libya) and Djanet (Algeria).

polities.name: Ghadames
polities.note: Caravan oasis governed by its own notables under Tunis/Tripoli suzerainty.

polities.name: Fezzan (Bornu suzerainty and local sheikhs)
polities.note: Between the Kanem conquest (13th c.) and the Awlad Muhammad; local Arab/Berber sheikhs at Traghan and Zawila.

polities.name: Awlad Muhammad of Fezzan
polities.note: Moroccan-origin sharifian dynasty at Murzuk; paid tribute to Tripoli; destroyed by the Karamanli 1811-13.

polities.name: Awlad Sulayman
polities.note: Arab tribe dominating the Sirte and Fezzan routes; under Abd al-Jalil Sayf al-Nasr ruled Fezzan c.1831-42; then migrated to Kanem.

polities.name: Senussi Order lands
polities.note: Sufi order whose zawiya network governed the Cyrenaican interior; moved to Kufra 1895 and Gouro (Chad) 1899; Italian conquest completed 1931.

polities.name: Kufra (Zuwaya)
polities.note: Zuwaya Arabs took the Kufra oases from the Tubu c.1840; became the Senussi capital 1895.

polities.name: Teda of Tibesti
polities.note: Teda clans under an elected derde (Tomagra clan); also ranged to Kawar and Kufra. French occupation 1914.

polities.name: Daza of Borkou and Ennedi
polities.note: Southern Tubu (Gorane) pastoralists; Senussi zawiyas from 1899; French 1913.

polities.name: Siwa oasis
polities.note: Self-governing Berber oasis under its shaykhs (eastern and western factions) until conquered by Muhammad Ali's Egypt 1820.

polities.name: Alaouite Sharifate of Tafilalt
polities.note: Alaouite sharifs (Moulay Ali al-Sharif, Muhammad ibn Sharif, al-Rashid) ruling Tafilalt before conquering Fez 1666; Tafilalt before 1631 under Saadis and Dila'iyya influence.

polities.name: Zawiya of Dila (Dila'iyya)
polities.note: Sufi lodge that ruled the Middle Atlas and, 1640s-1660s, Fez, Meknes and Salé; destroyed by al-Rashid 1668.

polities.name: Emirate of Tazerwalt (Iligh)
polities.note: Sidi Ali Bou Dmia's zawiya-state in the Anti-Atlas/Sous trading with Timbuktu (peak 1614-1670); autonomous again under the Hashim family in the 19th c. until Moulay Hassan's 1882/1886 harkas.

polities.name: Tekna confederation (Wad Nun)
polities.note: Arab-Berber tribal confederation of Wad Nun and the Draa mouth; the Beyrouk family of Guelmim acted as independent emirs in the 19th c., dealing with European merchants.

polities.name: Ait Atta confederation
polities.note: Amazigh 'five fifths' confederation of Jbel Saghro, Draa and Tafilalt fringes, outside makhzen control (bled es-siba) until the French Battle of Bougafer 1933; Ait Khabbash branch raided into Tuat.

polities.name: Reguibat
polities.note: Sahrawi camel-nomad confederation (Reguibat es-Sahel, Reguibat ech-Charg) of Saguia el-Hamra and the Hammada of Tindouf.

polities.name: Tindouf (Tajakant)
polities.note: Caravan town founded 1852 by the Tajakant tribe; destroyed by the Reguibat 1895.

polities.name: Ouled Delim
polities.note: Hassani warrior tribe of Rio de Oro (Tiris); Spanish coastal post Villa Cisneros 1884.

polities.name: Figuig oasis
polities.note: Seven ksour under their own jama'as; French pressure 1903.

polities.name: Golden Horde
polities.note: After the breakaway of Kazan (1438), Crimea (1441), Nogai, Astrakhan (1466) the rump 'Great Horde' held the lower Volga-Don steppe until destroyed by Crimea 1502.

polities.name: Nogai Horde
polities.note: Manghit beys between Volga, Yaik and Emba (north to Bashkiria). Split 1557 into Great Nogai (east of Volga) and Lesser Nogai (Kuban/Azov, Crimean vassal); Great Nogai displaced by the Kalmyks 1630s.

polities.name: Khanate of Kazan
polities.note: Khanate on the middle Volga and lower Kama; conquered by Muscovy 1552.

polities.name: Khanate of Astrakhan
polities.note: Lower Volga delta khanate; annexed by Muscovy 1556.

polities.name: Kalmyk Khanate
polities.note: Torghut Oirats who crossed the Yaik 1630; peak under Ayuka Khan (1669-1724); most left for Dzungaria 1771 and the khanate was abolished.

polities.name: Bashkir lands
polities.note: Bashkir tribes (four 'roads') holding votchina land rights under Russia; revolts 1662-64, 1704-11, 1735-40, 1755; Ufa fortress 1574. After 1800 increasingly settled by Russians.

polities.name: Bukey Horde
polities.note: Junior jüz Kazakhs allowed to settle between Volga and Ural; khan abolished 1845.

polities.name: Uzbek Khanate (Abu'l-Khayr)
polities.note: Abu'l-Khayr Khan's nomad confederation (Dasht-i Kipchak); collapsed at his death 1468, Kazakhs splitting off; descendants (Shaybanids) conquered Transoxiana 1500.

polities.name: Kazakh Khanate
polities.note: Founded by Janibek and Kerey in Semirechye; peak under Kasym (d.1521) and Tauke (1680-1715). After 1718/1723 (Dzungar 'Barefooted Flight') effectively three separate jüz, entered separately. 1847 = end of Kenesary's revolt.

polities.name: Senior Jüz (Uly Jüz)
polities.note: Semirechye and the Syr Darya middle; held Tashkent 1720s-1784 (Tole bi); Russian annexation 1846-48.

polities.name: Middle Jüz (Orta Jüz)
polities.note: Central and NE Kazakh steppe; Ablai Khan (r.1771-81) the dominant figure; khanship abolished by Speransky's 1822 Statute.

polities.name: Junior Jüz (Kishi Jüz)
polities.note: Western Kazakh steppe between Yaik/Ural, Aral Sea and Mangyshlak; Abulkhair's oath to Russia 1731; khan abolished 1824.

polities.name: Kenesary's Kazakh Khanate
polities.note: Revolt-state of Kenesary Kasymov across central Kazakhstan; killed by Kyrgyz 1847.

polities.name: Karakalpaks
polities.note: Lower Syr Darya, then the Amu Darya delta after 1740s; subject to Khiva in the 19th c.

polities.name: Timurid Empire
polities.note: Shah Rukh ruled from Herat; after 1447-1469 split into Samarkand (to 1500) and Herat (to 1507) branches, see separate entries.

polities.name: Timurid Samarkand (Transoxiana)
polities.note: Abu Sa'id and his sons (Sultan Ahmad, Babur briefly); fell to Muhammad Shaybani 1500-01.

polities.name: Timurid Herat (Khorasan)
polities.note: Sultan Husayn Bayqara's Khorasan; conquered by the Shaybanids 1507.

polities.name: Shaybanid Khanate of Bukhara
polities.note: Appanage system (Samarkand, Tashkent, Balkh, Bukhara); capital moved from Samarkand to Bukhara 1557 under Abdullah Khan II, who also held Herat and Khwarazm briefly.

polities.name: Janid (Ashtarkhanid) Khanate of Bukhara
polities.note: Balkh held as an appanage of the heir; real power passed to Manghit ataliqs from 1747.

polities.name: Emirate of Bukhara
polities.note: Lost Samarkand 1868 to Russia; gained Hissar/Kulob (1870s), Karategin, Darvaz (1877) and western Pamirs (1895).

polities.name: Khanate of Khiva
polities.note: Arabshahid Shibanids until 1727, then Inaqs (Qongrat dynasty from 1804); claimed suzerainty over Yomut and Teke Turkmen and the Karakalpaks.

polities.name: Khanate of Kokand
polities.note: Shahrukhid Ming dynasty of the Fergana Valley; Tashkent taken 1809, Kazakh Syr-Darya and Kyrgyz highlands by 1830s; Russia took Tashkent 1865, annexed rump 1876.

polities.name: Beylik of Shahrisabz
polities.note: Kenagas Uzbek beys of Shahrisabz and Kitab, frequently independent of Bukhara; Russian capture 1870 and handover to Bukhara.

polities.name: Beylik of Ura-Tyube
polities.note: Yuz Uzbek beylik contested by Bukhara and Kokand; Russian conquest 1866.

polities.name: Beylik of Hissar
polities.note: Uzbek (Yuz/Kongrat) beys of the Hissar valley; firmly under Bukhara from 1869.

polities.name: Beylik of Kulob
polities.note: Lakai/Kungrat Uzbek beys; absorbed by Bukhara 1870.

polities.name: Karategin (Mirs of Karategin)
polities.note: Tajik mountain principality of the Surkhob valley; annexed by Bukhara 1877.

polities.name: Darwaz (Shahs of Darwaz)
polities.note: Tajik shahs on both banks of the Panj; annexed by Bukhara 1878; left-bank portion went to Afghanistan.

polities.name: Shughnan-Roshan
polities.note: Pamiri principalities of the Panj valley; divided 1895 between Afghanistan and Bukhara (Russian).

polities.name: Wakhan (Mirs of Wakhan)
polities.note: Wakhi principality of the upper Panj; Afghan annexation 1883.

polities.name: Mirs of Badakhshan
polities.note: Yarid mirs (from c.1657) ruling Badakhshan; annexed by Abdur Rahman 1881. Before 1650s under Timurid/Shaybanid/Mughal princes.

polities.name: Hotak dynasty
polities.note: Ghilji revolt against the Safavids 1709; conquered Isfahan 1722; expelled from Persia 1729; Kandahar taken by Nader Shah 1738.

polities.name: Abdali Sultanate of Herat
polities.note: Abdali (later Durrani) Pashtun revolt-state at Herat between Safavid collapse and Nader Shah's conquest (1729-32).

polities.name: Durrani Empire
polities.note: Ahmad Shah Durrani: Afghanistan, Kashmir, Punjab, Sindh and Baluchistan tributary, Khorasan protectorate; Punjab lost to the Sikhs 1760s-1799; Kashmir 1819; Sadozai collapse 1818-23.

polities.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
polities.note: Dost Mohammad Khan; Balkh 1850, Kandahar 1855, Herat 1863; Badakhshan 1881, Hazarajat 1893, Kafiristan 1896. Shah Shuja's British-backed restoration 1839-42.

polities.name: Principality of Herat
polities.note: Sadozai remnant under Mahmud Shah and Kamran (to 1842), then Yar Mohammad Alakozai; besieged by Persia 1837-38 and 1856; taken by Dost Mohammad 1863.

polities.name: Kandahar Sardars
polities.note: Barakzai 'Dil brothers' (Purdil, Kohandil, Rahmdil Khan); British occupation 1839-42; annexed by Kabul 1855.

polities.name: Peshawar Sardars
polities.note: Barakzai brothers (Yar Mohammad, Sultan Mohammad); annexed by Ranjit Singh 1834.

polities.name: Khanate of Kunduz (Qataghan)
polities.note: Qataghan Uzbek mirs; peak under Mir Murad Beg (c.1815-1842) who also ruled Badakhshan and Balkh; Afghan conquest 1859.

polities.name: Khanate of Maymana
polities.note: Ming Uzbek khans; strongest of the 'Chahar Wilayat'; final Afghan conquest 1884.

polities.name: Uzbek khanates of Andkhoy, Shibirghan and Sar-e Pol
polities.note: Remaining small Uzbek khanates of the 'Four Wilayats' (with Maymana) in the northern Afghan plain; Afghan by 1875.

polities.name: Khanate of Balkh
polities.note: Appanage of Shaybanid and Janid heirs; Afghan from 1751, then autonomous Uzbek rulers under Bukharan influence; annexed by Dost Mohammad 1850 (Mazar-i Sharif became the seat).

polities.name: Kafiristan
polities.note: Non-Muslim Kalasha/Kati/Prasun-speaking valley communities never subject to a state until Abdur Rahman's conquest 1895-96 (renamed Nuristan).

polities.name: Hazarajat
polities.note: Autonomous Hazara mirs and tribes of the central highlands; conquered by Abdur Rahman 1891-93.

polities.name: Tekke Turkmen
polities.note: Akhal oasis Tekke, and from 1856 Merv Tekke (defeated Persia 1861); Russian victories at Geok Tepe 1881 and Merv annexation 1884.

polities.name: Yomut Turkmen
polities.note: Two branches: Khwarazm Yomut (Khiva oasis edge) and Gorgan-Atrek Yomut on the Persian frontier; Krasnovodsk 1869.

polities.name: Goklen Turkmen
polities.note: Upper Gorgan valley, most often tributary to Persia.

polities.name: Ersari Turkmen
polities.note: Middle Amu Darya and northern Afghanistan (Andkhoy area).

polities.name: Salor Turkmen
polities.note: Oldest Oghuz Turkmen tribe; held Merv until c.1830, then Serakhs; broken by the Tekke and Persians.

polities.name: Saryk Turkmen
polities.note: Held Merv until displaced by the Tekke 1856; then the Murghab at Panjdeh (Russian 1885).

polities.name: Moghulistan
polities.note: Nomadic Chagatai khanate (Semirechye, Ili, Tarim north); Dughlat emirs ruled Kashgar; split 1462 into western (Moghulistan proper, to 1514/1680s) and eastern (Turpan) khanates.

polities.name: Turpan Khanate
polities.note: Eastern Chagatai branch (Yunus's son Ahmad; separate from c.1462/1487); took Hami 1513; Wikipedia gives 1487-c.1660 for the khanate, after which Turpan fell to Yarkent/Dzungar control (1680).

polities.name: Yarkent Khanate
polities.note: Sultan Said Khan's Moghul khanate of the western Tarim (Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu); Dzungar conquest 1680 installed Afaqi khojas.

polities.name: Kashgaria under the Khojas
polities.note: Naqshbandi khoja factions as Dzungar vassals; Qing conquest 1759 (Altishahr then under Qing until 1865).

polities.name: Kumul Khanate
polities.note: Uyghur khanate of Hami, early Qing ally; abolished 1930.

polities.name: Yettishar
polities.note: Yakub Beg's Kokandi-led state over the Tarim basin (and Turpan/Urumqi 1870-77); Qing reconquest 1877.

polities.name: Kyrgyz tribes
polities.note: Tribal Kyrgyz (right and left wings, Ichkilik) of the Tian Shan and Pamir-Alay, in Tian Shan from the 15th-16th c.; Bugu, Sarybagysh, Solto tribes accepted Russian rule 1855-67.

polities.name: Russian Siberia (effective ostrog control)
polities.note: Effective reach of the ostrog/yasak network (not claims): Tobolsk 1587, Mangazeya 1601, Tomsk 1604, Yeniseysk 1619, Krasnoyarsk 1628, Yakutsk 1632, Okhotsk 1647, Anadyr 1649, Irkutsk 1661, Nerchinsk 1689, Kamchatka 1697-1731, Omsk 1716, Amur 1858-60. Native nations below remained largely self-governing under yasak; Chukchi effectively outside control. Overlay native polities on top.

polities.name: Khanate of Sibir
polities.note: Taibugid then Shibanid (Kuchum, 1563-98) khanate of the Irtysh-Tobol; Yermak took Qashliq 1582; Kuchum defeated 1598.

polities.name: Tyumen Khanate
polities.note: Shibanid/Taibugid khanate on the Tura; Abu'l-Khayr held it 1428-46; succeeded by the Khanate of Sibir.

polities.name: Pelym Principality
polities.note: Mansi (Vogul) principality on the Tavda/Pelym and Lozva; raided Perm; Russian ostrog 1593.

polities.name: Koda Principality
polities.note: Khanty principality of the Alachev princes on the lower Ob; allied with Russia from 1585, abolished 1644.

polities.name: Obdor Principality
polities.note: Khanty-Nenets princes (Taishin family) of the lower Ob; Obdorsk ostrog 1595.

polities.name: Piebald Horde (Pegaya Orda)
polities.note: Selkup chiefdom-confederation of the middle Ob (Prince Voni); Narym ostrog 1596-98.

polities.name: Nenets (Samoyeds)
polities.note: Reindeer-herding tundra clans from the Kanin peninsula to the Yenisei; Pustozersk 1499, Mangazeya 1601; 'forest Nenets' further south.

polities.name: Evenks (Tungus)
polities.note: Clan-based reindeer hunters across the central Siberian taiga from the Yenisei to the Okhotsk sea; yasak from 1620s; Manchu-allied Evenk/Solon on the Amur are East Asia.

polities.name: Sakha (Yakuts)
polities.note: Turkic horse/cattle herders of the middle Lena under clan toyons (Tygyn of Kangalas the best known); Yakutsk ostrog 1632, revolts 1634-42; later spread north to the Kolyma and Anabar.

polities.name: Evens (Lamuts)
polities.note: Reindeer herders of the Verkhoyansk-Kolyma uplands and Okhotsk coast.

polities.name: Yukaghirs
polities.note: Once spanning Lena-Anadyr; heavily reduced by epidemics and wars after Russian arrival (Nizhnekolymsk 1644).

polities.name: Chukchi
polities.note: Reindeer and coastal Chukchi defeated Russian campaigns (Pavlutsky killed 1747); Anadyr ostrog abandoned 1764; nominal submission 1778 but self-governing to the Soviet period. Extent clipped at 180 deg: the territory continues east to Cape Dezhnev (66.1N, -169.7).

polities.name: Koryaks
polities.note: Reindeer and maritime Koryaks of northern Kamchatka and the Penzhina; subdued 1700-1757.

polities.name: Itelmens (Kamchadals)
polities.note: Fortified-village peoples of southern Kamchatka; Atlasov 1697, great revolt 1731; drastic population collapse.

polities.name: Buryats
polities.note: Mongol-speaking clans (Bulagat, Ekhirit, Khori, Khongodor) west and east of Baikal; Russian ostrogs Bratsk 1631, Irkutsk 1661, Udinsk 1666; border fixed at Kyakhta 1727.

polities.name: Tuvan lands (Uriankhai)
polities.note: Turkic herders and taiga reindeer hunters (Todzha) of the upper Yenisei, organised under Qing into five khoshuns.

polities.name: Yenisei Kirghiz (Khongorai)
polities.note: Four Kirghiz uluses (Altysar, Isar, Altyr, Tuba) on the upper Yenisei fighting Russian Krasnoyarsk; most deported to Dzungaria 1703.

polities.name: Teleuts and Altai Oirats
polities.note: Teleut ('White Kalmyk') princes (Abak) of the upper Ob and Altai Telengits; Russian after the fall of Dzungaria (1756).

polities.name: Northern Yuan
polities.note: Great khans of the eastern Mongols; Oirat dominance 1438-54 (Esen); reunified by Dayan Khan c.1480-1517; after 1550 the khan's direct domain shrank to the Chahar, Khalkha/Tumed being autonomous; Ligdan Khan's death 1634/35 ended it.

polities.name: Four Oirat
polities.note: Choros, Torghut, Dörbet, Khoshut confederation of western Mongolia; under Esen Taishi (1438-54) ruled all Mongolia and captured the Ming emperor (1449). Succeeded by the Dzungar Khanate, Khoshut Khanate and Kalmyks.

polities.name: Dzungar Khanate
polities.note: Choros-led Oirat empire (Erdeni Batur, Galdan Boshugtu, Tsewang Rabtan, Galdan Tseren); Tarim vassals 1680-1757, Kazakh tribute 1723-58, occupied Lhasa 1717-20; destroyed by the Qing 1755-58.

polities.name: Khoshut Khanate
polities.note: Güshi Khan's Khoshut conquered Kham and Tsang (1637-42) and made the 5th Dalai Lama ruler of Tibet under Khoshut overlordship; Lha-bzang Khan killed by the Dzungars 1717.

polities.name: Upper Mongols of Kokonor (Khoshut of Qinghai)
polities.note: Güshi Khan's sons' banners around Kokonor; Lobzang Danjin's revolt 1723-24 crushed and organised into Qing banners (to 1911).

polities.name: Tüsheet Khan Aimag
polities.note: Central Khalkha khanate (Abtai Khan founded Erdene Zuu 1585); Galdan's invasion 1688 drove Khalkha to submit to the Qing at Dolon Nor 1691; Sain Noyon split off 1725.

polities.name: Setsen Khan Aimag
polities.note: Eastern Khalkha khanate.

polities.name: Zasagt Khan Aimag
polities.note: Western Khalkha khanate; conflict with Tüsheet Khan triggered Galdan's intervention 1688.

polities.name: Sain Noyon Khan Aimag
polities.note: Created by the Qing from Tüsheet Khan lands for Tseren Efu.

polities.name: Altan Khans of the Khotogoid
polities.note: Northwestern Khalkha khans (Sholoi Ubashi, Ombo Erdene) overlords of Tuva and the Yenisei Kirghiz; dealt with Moscow; crushed by Dzungars c.1690.

polities.name: Tumed (Altan Khan)
polities.note: Altan Khan (r.1542-82) founded Hohhot 1572, invited the 3rd Dalai Lama 1578; overrun by Ligdan 1628-32, then Manchu banners.

polities.name: Ordos Mongols
polities.note: Jinong's tumen inside the Yellow River loop; Qing league (Yeke Juu) after 1636.

polities.name: Phagmodrupa dynasty
polities.note: Lang family gongmas who ended Sakya rule; Tsang lost to the Rinpungpa after 1435, real power gone by 1565; Nedong taken by the Tsangpa 1618.

polities.name: Rinpungpa
polities.note: Ministers of the Phagmodrupa who ruled Tsang from Rinpung and Samdrubtse; held Lhasa 1498-1517; overthrown by their governor Karma Tseten (Tsangpa) 1565.

polities.name: Tsangpa dynasty
polities.note: Karma-Kagyu-backed kings of Tsang; conquered Ü 1618; defeated by Güshi Khan 1642.

polities.name: Ganden Phodrang
polities.note: Dalai Lamas' government; western Tibet (Ngari) from 1683; eastern Kham states mostly self-ruling (see Kham entries); Nyarong added 1865.

polities.name: Principality of Gyantse
polities.note: Rabten Kunsang Phag's principality (Gyantse Kumbum 1427); absorbed by the Rinpungpa.

polities.name: Lato Lho (Shekar)
polities.note: Myriarchy-descended princes of western Tsang under Phagmodrupa/Rinpungpa suzerainty.

polities.name: Gungthang
polities.note: Descendants of the Yarlung kings controlling the Kyirong-Nepal route; conquered by the Tsangpa c.1620.

polities.name: Lhagyari
polities.note: Small hereditary kingdom in southern Tibet claiming Yarlung royal descent; autonomous estate under Lhasa.

polities.name: Kingdom of Pome (Powo)
polities.note: Kanam Depa rulers of Powo, largely independent until Lhasa's 1931 conquest.

polities.name: Guge Kingdom
polities.note: Western Tibetan kingdom (with Purang); Jesuit mission 1624; conquered by Ladakh 1630.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ladakh
polities.note: Held Guge and Ngari 1630-84 until the Tibet-Ladakh-Mughal war (Treaty of Tingmosgang 1684); conquered by Zorawar Singh 1834-42.

polities.name: Kingdom of Lo (Mustang)
polities.note: Founded by Ame Pal c.1380; tributary to Gorkha Nepal from 1789.

polities.name: Kingdom of Derge
polities.note: Most powerful Kham kingdom; Dêgê seat from the mid-15th c.; printing house 1729; annexed by Zhao Erfeng 1908-09.

polities.name: Kingdom of Nangchen
polities.note: Kingdom of 25 tribes in upper Mekong (Dza-chu) basin under the Nangchen gyalpo.

polities.name: Kingdom of Lingtsang
polities.note: Small kingdom north-east of Derge claiming descent from Gesar of Ling.

polities.name: Kingdom of Chakla
polities.note: One of the four great Kham chiefdoms (with Derge, Batang, Lithang); Ming recognition 1407; Qing annexation 1911.

polities.name: Chiefdom of Batang
polities.note: Hereditary chiefdom on the Jinsha; 1905 uprising led to Zhao Erfeng's conquest.

polities.name: Chiefdom of Lithang
polities.note: Birthplace of the 7th Dalai Lama; Qing tusi from 1719.

polities.name: Chamdo (Phagpa Lha lama state)
polities.note: Gelug monastic principality of Jampaling (founded 1437) under the Phagpa Lha incarnations.

polities.name: Hor States (Five Hor)
polities.note: Five Mongol-descended chiefdoms of the Yalong valley; Beri king defeated by Güshi Khan 1639/40.

polities.name: Nyarong (Gönpo Namgyal)
polities.note: Gönpo Namgyal's chiefdom expanded over Derge, Hor and Lithang c.1848-63; destroyed by a Lhasa army 1865, after which Nyarong was governed by a Lhasa commissioner.

polities.name: Chuchen (Great Jinchuan)
polities.note: Gyalrong chiefdom whose wars with the Qing (1747-49, 1771-76) were among the costliest Qing campaigns; with Tsanlha (Small Jinchuan, 31.0N 102.36E) annexed 1776.

polities.name: Gyalrong chiefdoms
polities.note: The 'eighteen' Gyalrong chiefdoms (Somo, Chogtse, Dzonggag, Trokyab, etc.) of the upper Dadu basin; Great and Small Jinchuan listed separately.

polities.name: Muli lama kingdom
polities.note: Gelug lama-kings (founded after the 3rd Dalai Lama's visit, 1580).

polities.name: Golog confederation
polities.note: Three Golog chiefly lineages (Wangchen Bum, Akyong Bum, Khangsar) of the upper Yellow River, effectively independent.

gaps.area: Najd oasis towns before 1744 (al-Washm, Sudair, al-Kharj, al-Aflaj, Huraymila, Ushaiqer)
gaps.note: Not empty: dozens of autonomous oasis emirates of a few towns each (e.g. Al Madlaj of Majma'ah, Huraymila, al-Kharj), surrounded by Bedouin dirahs. Only Uyaynah, Diriyah and Riyadh itemised; fill the rest of central Najd with the Bedouin confederations listed or leave fragmented.

gaps.area: Asir highlands and Tihamat Asir before 1800
gaps.note: Tribal (Shahran, Rufaydah, Bal-Qarn, Ghamid, Zahran) with nominal allegiance to the Sharifs of Mecca or the Zaydi imams; Abu Arish/Jizan coast held by the Sharifs of Abu Arish (Khayrati) under the Zaydi imams in the 17th-18th c.

gaps.area: Rub' al-Khali interior
gaps.note: Largely uninhabited sand sea; Al Murrah and Rashid/Manahil nomads only on its margins.

gaps.area: Nafud desert and northern Arabia 1400-1650
gaps.note: Tribal (Anazzah, Shammar, Banu Lam) with no state; al-Jawf/Dumat al-Jandal and Tayma small oasis communities.

gaps.area: Upper Yemen tribal belt (Hashid and Bakil, al-Jawf, Marib)
gaps.note: Tribal confederations (Hashid, Bakil, Dahm, Abidah of Marib, Sharifs of al-Jawf/Marib) under nominal Zaydi or Ottoman suzerainty; fill from the Zaydi Imamate/Qasimid entries.

gaps.area: Interior Oman and Dhahirah (Buraimi, Ibri, Sharqiyah)
gaps.note: Under Nabhani maliks/Ibadi imams then Ya'rubid and Busaidi rulers, but tribes (Bani Ghafir, Hinawi and Ghafiri factions, Duru', Wahiba, Janaba) often autonomous; Buraimi contested with Saudis 1800-1869.

gaps.area: Dhofar 1400-1829
gaps.note: Under Kathiri sultans intermittently from 1414, otherwise Qara/Shahra tribes; Busaidi Oman from 1829 (firm 1879).

gaps.area: Libyan Desert (Great Sand Sea, Calanshio, Sarir) and Tanezrouft/Erg Chech
gaps.note: Effectively uninhabited sand seas and regs; crossed by caravans only.

gaps.area: Draa valley and pre-Saharan Morocco south of the High Atlas
gaps.note: Ksour of the Draa (Ktaoua, Mhamid, Zagora), Dades and Todgha under local jama'as, Arab tribes (Ma'qil) and the Ait Atta/Ait Yafelman; nominally Saadi/Alaouite. Fill with Ait Atta and Morocco.

gaps.area: Sahara of Algeria between Tuat and the Tell (Grand Erg Occidental, Saoura)
gaps.note: Saoura ksour (Beni Abbes, Kenadsa zawiya) and nomads (Doui Menia, Ouled Djerir, Ghenanma); nominally Moroccan.

gaps.area: Ennedi/Wanyanga and the Libya-Chad-Sudan border (Uweinat)
gaps.note: Sparse Bideyat/Zaghawa and Tubu pastoralists; Wadai and Darfur claims on the southern edge.

gaps.area: Ustyurt plateau and Kyzylkum / Karakum desert interiors
gaps.note: Very thinly used winter pastures of Kazakh (Adai), Turkmen (Chowdur, Igdir) and Karakalpak nomads; no fixed authority. Draw as the adjoining nomad confederation or leave empty.

gaps.area: Betpak-Dala desert (central Kazakhstan)
gaps.note: Near-empty clay desert between Chu and Sarysu rivers; seasonal Kazakh use only.

gaps.area: Eastern Pamirs (Alichur, Murghab plateau)
gaps.note: High plateau with seasonal Kyrgyz herders; nominally Kokand/Qing/Shughnan until the 1895 Pamir boundary.

gaps.area: Taklamakan desert interior and Lop Nur
gaps.note: Uninhabited sand sea within the oases-states' outlines.

gaps.area: Taimyr peninsula and Anabar tundra
gaps.note: Nganasan, Dolgan and Enets hunters; no polity (Russian yasak via Khatanga from 17th c.).

gaps.area: Arctic coast and islands (Severnaya Zemlya, New Siberian Islands)
gaps.note: Uninhabited.

gaps.area: Lower Amur, Okhotsk-Uda and Sakhalin hinterland
gaps.note: Nivkh, Ulch, Nanai and Negidal fisher-peoples under nominal Ming/Qing (Nurgan) then Russian (1858-60) authority; expected in the East Asia list.

gaps.area: Upper Kolyma - Chukotka interior uplands
gaps.note: Very sparse Yukaghir/Even/Chukchi seasonal use; boundaries between those nations are approximate.

gaps.area: Changtang plateau (northern Tibet)
gaps.note: Mostly uninhabited high plateau; nomad pastures (Hor, Nagchu) on its south edge under Lhasa; northern part empty.

gaps.area: Gobi desert core and Alashan
gaps.note: Sparse; Alashan Khoshut banner (Qing jasagh from 1697) in the west, Khalkha and Inner Mongol banners elsewhere; Ejin Torghut 1698-.

gaps.area: Kham states not itemised (Lhatok, Gonjo, Draya, Markham, Sangen, Gyelthang)
gaps.note: Small chiefdoms and monastic estates between Chamdo, Derge and Batang; fill with the nearest itemised Kham polity or Ganden Phodrang.

gaps.area: Amdo outside Kokonor and Golog (Rebgong, Labrang, Ngawa)
gaps.note: Monastic estates (Labrang Tashikyil 1709) and tribal chiefdoms under Xining/Ming-Qing tusi; expected partly in the East Asia list.
